texts.facts: In the accident, claimant suffered grievous injuries. Claimant filed MVC No.6708/2012 before the Tribunal claiming compensation of Rs.1,00,00,000/- from the respondents contending that accident occurred due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry, due to the accidental injures, he has suffered permanent physical disability, he was earning Rs.50,000/- per month from his business. The Tribunal considered permanent physical disability of the claimant at 25%, assessed his income at Rs.2,80,000/- per annum, applied 13 multiplier and assessed his future income at Rs.9,10,000/-. The compensation was held payable by both insurers i.e., respondent Nos.2 and 5 equally. Therefore, finding of the Tribunal on the point of negligence is contrary to the evidence on record and the same is liable to be [LEAKAGE_MASK]. Claimant was admittedly running partnership business. According to him, compensation awarded on other heads is also on the higher side. Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in fixing 50% liability to the insurer of Tempo Traveller vehicle. On investigation, chargesheet Ex.P2 was filed against driver of Sri Kumar B C vs Sri Manjunatha on 27 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/54344009/ 7 the lorry for the offences - 11 - NC: 2024:KHC:48704-DB punishable under Sections 279, 337, 338 IPC and under Section 134 (a)(b) read with Section 187 Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short 'MV Act'). Case against lorry driver was registered in C.C.No.184/2013 and driver of the lorry pleaded guilty in the said case. Learned Magistrate convicted and sentenced him for the offences punishable under Sections, 279,337,338 IPC and 134(a)(b) read with Section 187 MV Act.
texts.arguments: Therefore, there is no loss of future earning. Compensation awarded on that head is unsustainable. 9. Sri O Mahesh, learned Counsel representing Royal Sundaram Allianz Insurance Company Ltd., (respondent No.2 before the Tribunal) submits that chargesheet and fact of driver of the lorry pleading guilty are not conclusive proof. He justifies the award.

This Court by the judgment dated 09.09.2015 set aside the judgment under challenge and remanded the matter to the Tribunal with direction to implead respondent Nos.4 to 6 in the case and for reconsideration of the matter thereafter.
7. The Tribunal on hearing the parties by the impugned award held that both driver of the lorry and Tempo Traveller contributed 50% each in occurrence of accident.
The Tribunal considered permanent physical disability of the claimant at 25%, assessed his income at Rs.2,80,000/- per annum, applied 13 multiplier and assessed his future income at Rs.9,10,000/-.

The Tribunal in all awarded compensation of Rs.21,00,000/- on different heads as below:

Analysis Reg. Negligence:
11. Parties have not disputed that on 07.08.2012 at 12:45 a.m., when claimant was traveling in Tempo Traveller bearing registration No.K.A-01-AB-2638, an accident took place involving the said Tempo Traveller and
It is also not disputed that regarding the accident, Ms.Shilpa-family member of the claimant, filed complaint as per Ex.P1 against the driver of the lorry.
Learned Magistrate convicted and sentenced him for the offences punishable under Sections, 279,337,338 IPC and 134(a)(b) read with Section 187 MV Act.
By such evidence, there was prima-facie proof of occurrence of accident due to actionable negligence on the part of the driver of the lorry.
It is no doubt true that those documents were not conclusive proof, but they have some presumptive value under Section 114 illustration (e) of Evidence Act.
Therefore, it was for respondent Nos.1 and 2 to adduce evidence to rebut the said presumption.
Insurer of lorry /respondent No.2 had challenged first award of the Tribunal before this Court in MFA No.5268/2014 C/w MFA No.6048/2014 on the same ground.
This Court on setting aside the order of Tribunal, remanded the matter for fresh consideration, reserving liberty to the parties to lead evidence.
Even thereafter respondent Nos.1 and 2 did not avail the said opportunity to lead evidence.

12. Regulation No.8 of the Regulations,1989 state that whenever a driver of the motor vehicle is nearing a road - 12 - NC: 2024:KHC:48704-DB intersection, pedestrian crossing, or road junction, he shall not enter such intersection, junctio
Regulation No.9 of the Regulations,1989 is to the same effect relating to junction where the traffic is not being regulated.
It says he has to give way to all traffic approaching the intersection on his right hand.
Before this Court it is being contended that the driver of the Tempo Traveller entered the road without taking any due care as required under Regulation Nos.8 and 9 of the Regulations,1989.
The sketch/Ex.P3 shows that lorry has proceeded from its extreme right side to extreme left side.
When driver of the lorry pleaded guilty, it was for respondent Nos.1 to 3 to enter witness box and claim that driver of Tempo Traveller was negligent.
But they did not defend the case at all, nor respondent Nos.1 and 2 examined respondent No.3/driver of lorry.
That amounts to suppression of available material evidence, which leads to drawing of adverse inference against respondent Nos.1 to 3.
The Tribunal without assigning any acceptable reasons has come to the conclusion that the drivers of both vehicles have contributed to the occurrence of accident, which is wholly unsustainable.
Hence, the said finding requires - 13 - NC: 2024:KHC:48704-DB to be set aside and the entire culpable negligence has to be imputed to respondent No.3 and vicariously respondent No.1.

He underwent debridement of wound, abdominal flap and split skin grafting by plastic surgeons on 10.08.2012.

Thus PW2's evidence shows that claimant was treated as inpatient in the said hospital between 07.08.2012 to 05.10.2012 and again between 29.11.2012 to 30.11.2012.

The original proceedings are of the year 2012.
This Court remanded the matter on 09.09.2015 directing the Tribunal to give opportunity to both the parties, reserving liberty to both the parties to lead evidence.
Even that opportunity was not availed by the claimant.
Under the aforesaid circumstances, the production of said documents cannot be allowed.

As per Ex.P15, the income of the claimant for the assessment year 2012-13 was Rs.2,76,112/-.

on deducting tax of Rs.8,029/- paid for those two years, his average income of two years comes to Rs.4,41,373 / 2 = Rs.2,20,686.5 rounded off to Rs.2,20,687/-.

Having regard to the age,
employment, disability of the claimant and the judgment of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1, 25% has to be added to his income by way of future prospects.
Therefore, his annual income comes to Rs.2,75,859/-.
Applicable multiplier is 13 and disability to be considered is 50%.

Therefore, loss of future income comes to (Rs.2,75,859 x 13 x 50%) = Rs.17,93,083/-.
